accuracy.evidence: Matches KS1 human body / air needs: nose or mouth → windpipe → lungs; oxygen in; carbon dioxide out; chest rise/fall with breath.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets breathe-out-as-oxygen, air-stops-at-mouth, windpipe/food-tube mix-ups, and ignored chest movement in predictions, challenge why(), and adult notes.

lab_distinct.evidence: Lab is airway path and gas exchange — distinct from heart pump/vessels (flagheart) and from living-needs sorting (flagneeds).

lab_teaches.evidence: Learner builds the path, chooses gases, moves the chest, and completes the story before confirmation text.

predictions.evidence: Wrong options (ear canal; only CO2 in; chest disappears) are the slips the following task overturns.

challenge_feedback.evidence: why() names ankle/finger entry, food-tube confusion, out-breath-as-oxygen, and locked-chest slips specifically.

readability.evidence: Ages 5–7 wording: short kid lines, concrete chest and path language.

no_filler.evidence: No delve/journey phrasing; each line teaches path, gas, or chest movement.

mobile.evidence: Chest In/Out and path Next controls stay large at 390 px; nothing clipped on iPhone walkthrough screenshots.

accessibility.evidence: Path, gas and chest steps all have button twins beside drag/tap; say() updates the canvas aria-label each move; challenge feedback uses aria-live status.

sources: UK National Curriculum 2013 Science KS1: Animals including humans — basic needs for survival (air) and body parts
BBC Bitesize KS1: The human body — breathing, lungs, oxygen and carbon dioxide
